text:
Waitlist state for 13 Open campuses. Slack, 2026-10-05.

MacKenzie Price, 10:19 AM (the instruction):

"Please update the website with the following locations now on Waitlist: Austin High School, Boca Raton, Boston,
Dorado, New York, Palo Alto, Park City, Plano, Raleigh, San Francisco, Scottsdale, The Woodlands, Tulsa."

That is 13 campuses, and it matches exactly the 13 HubSpot Programs carrying the new website_campus_intro wording
read on 2026-10-05. "Austin High School" is the Alpha High School Program (26445615147); "New York" is the Alpha
Anywhere Center Program (26463204876, https://alpha.school/new-york-city/).

Rachel Goodlad (admissions), same thread, setting the policy:

- The admissions process does not change. Families still complete the existing application; they should simply know
  there is no immediate enrolment. "Basically you should announce this but I do not believe the process should
  change."
- It applies to this school year, 2026-27.
- It is a campus-level announcement, not a per-family state shown on the site: "There are plenty on a waitlist for
  various reasons and we don't distinguish online."
- She rejected the first draft wording as negative: "apply for future enrollment" replaces "immediate enrollment is
  unavailable", and the word "basis" was dropped. She approved the final wording: "Sounds awkward but I think this is
  ok right now."
- Yash Chitneni asked her, in his numbered questions, whether a campus-level HubSpot setting should be added: "We
  found 'Waitlisted' on individual admissions records, but no dedicated campus waitlist switch. Should we add a
  campus-level setting in HubSpot to manage this consistently?" She answered his other questions and left that one
  unanswered, so the ask is live with admissions and outstanding.

Yash Chitneni, same thread, what he changed on each of the 13 pages (four coordinated elements, not one sentence):

- the top banner application button now reads "Apply for waitlist";
- the introductory copy carries the approved sentence;
- the resources section near tuition and contact uses waitlist wording on its application buttons;
- the enrolment graphic at the top of the page (the intro card) is updated to say "Apply for Waitlist".

Matt Barge, relaying and confirming to the website agent:

"the waitlist is correct. that's straight from MacKenzie, so the base rule needs to change. we never had waitlist
stuff before."

Context the agent put to him: on 2026-10-02 HubSpot integration 46546260 rewrote website_campus_intro on those 13
Open Programs in two passes (18:16Z and 19:25Z) from "[DISPLAY_NAME] is open and enrolling." to "[DISPLAY_NAME] is
open, and we're accepting applications for our 2026-27 waitlist. Apply for future enrollment, and our admissions team
will guide you through the next steps." The other 33 Open Programs still read "is open and enrolling." The observer
filed 13 tickets against check bundle 1.10 row campus.intro.status-source, because that rule accepted only the
enrolling sentence for an Open campus.
